requirements.summary: An endpoint may run moq-lite over a reliable byte-stream transport via Qmux when UDP is unavailable.
requirements.rationale: A permission: a publisher that never uses Qmux is conforming, so there is nothing to fail. The L1 runner listens only on bare QUIC and WebTransport (bindings 1 and 2), so Qmux bindings 3 and 4 are not exercised.

requirements.summary: Both endpoints should begin sending and receiving streams as soon as the connection is established, without an extra round-trip.
requirements.rationale: The publisher's Setup stream and its answers to early requests are judged by the setup and announce scenarios, but "right away" has no deadline: whether a publisher waited internally is indistinguishable from scheduling and network delay, so a verdict would rest on a timing guess. The runner's own session must not wait for the publisher's SETUP before opening its request streams.

requirements.summary: Each endpoint opens one unidirectional Setup Stream at session start, sends exactly one SETUP message on it and closes it with FIN.
requirements.rationale: The publisher's half is observable on every session: after accepting the connection the runner records the publisher's unidirectional streams and checks that one carries the Setup STREAM_TYPE, decodes as exactly one SETUP (L1b codec, empty parameter list allowed) and ends with FIN rather than a reset or further bytes. The runner must itself open, fill and FIN its own Setup stream the same way. A SETUP whose framing is intact and whose only defect is a repeated Parameter ID counts as decoded for this row; the duplicate is judged by L06-7-3-MUST-NOT-111 alone, so one defect never fails both rows.

requirements.summary: An endpoint buffers any stream whose behavior or encoding depends on a negotiated extension until the peer's SETUP has arrived.
requirements.rationale: Buffering is internal and the only extension-dependent streams of this draft (Probe and other optional capabilities) are out of the L1 scope, so the runner opens none and negotiates none; nothing on the wire distinguishes a buffering publisher. The runner's own session must likewise hold any extension stream from the publisher until the publisher's SETUP has been decoded.

requirements.summary: A relay does not forward SETUP to another hop, because each session negotiates its capabilities independently.
requirements.rationale: The obligation is on relays; the implementation under test is an origin publisher whose session ends at the runner, so there is no next hop to forward SETUP to.

requirements.summary: A receiving application should process or buffer Groups that arrive out of order rather than block on flow control.
requirements.rationale: This is a receiver obligation: the runner plays the subscriber, so it applies to the runner, not to the publisher under test. The runner must itself accept Group streams in any order and keep reading all of them, so that out-of-order arrival never stalls a publisher on flow control or turns into a false Fail.

requirements.summary: A publisher may send a small single-frame Group as a QUIC datagram when reliability is not required.
requirements.rationale: A permission with nothing to fail, and datagrams are out of the L1 scope. The runner must tolerate (ignore or record) datagrams on bindings 1 and 2 and must not count a Group delivered that way as missing from its stream evidence without saying so.

requirements.summary: A publisher may start a Group stream at a frame index above 0 when it holds, or was asked for, only part of the Group.
requirements.rationale: A permission; its limit (a partial Group only for a subscriber that asked for one) is judged under L06-3-6-MUST-020. The runner's GROUP decoding must accept a non-zero Frame Start and number the following FRAMEs from it.

requirements.summary: A publisher that cannot serve a Group from the requested frame skips that Group and starts the subscription at the beginning of a later Group instead of delivering the part it holds.
requirements.rationale: Observable from the GROUP headers of the publisher's Group streams, using the draft's abutting pattern (Section 3.6): the runner first subscribes with Group Start = G, Group End = G and Frame End = N-1 and receives frames 0 through N-1 of Group G, then subscribes with Group Start = G and Frame Start = N, so the non-zero Frame Start names a Group the runner has received, as the draft requires. The first Group stream of the second subscription must be Group G at Frame Start exactly N, or a later Group at Frame Start 0 when the publisher cannot serve G from frame N; any other Position is a Fail. A separate default subscription must never receive a non-zero Frame Start. Both conforming outcomes are accepted, so the evaluator never depends on whether the publisher still holds Group G. The draft is inconsistent on the Group Start encoding: Section 3.6 (draft 414-416) and moq.dev (lite/subscribe.rs decode_start_group) carry the raw value, while draft 2056-2058 says Group Start is offset by 1. The runner sends the raw G; a first Group of exactly G-1 at Frame Start N (compliant only under the offset reading) is recorded as the reading conflict and makes the row inconclusive (NotRun) rather than a Fail.

requirements.summary: A subscriber that has not received the Group named by Group Start sends Frame Start = 0.
requirements.rationale: This constrains the SUBSCRIBE a subscriber sends; the runner plays the subscriber, so it does not apply to the publisher under test. The runner must itself comply without exception: it sends Frame Start 0 unless it has already received frames of the Group that Group Start names, which happens only in the abutting second subscription of the L06-3-6-MUST-020 probe.

requirements.summary: An unbounded subscription (Group End = 0) sends Frame End = 0.
requirements.rationale: This constrains the SUBSCRIBE a subscriber sends; the runner plays the subscriber, so it does not apply to the publisher under test. The runner must itself send Frame End 0 whenever Group End is 0; its single deliberate exception is the invalid-bounds probe that exists to judge the publisher under L06-3-6-MUST-023.

requirements.summary: A publisher treats a SUBSCRIBE that violates the Frame Start or Frame End rule as a protocol violation and resets the subscription stream.
requirements.rationale: The runner sends a SUBSCRIBE with Group End = 0 and a non-zero Frame End (the only violation a publisher can detect from the message alone, since it cannot know which Groups the subscriber has received). The draft says "reset the stream" and uses session-level wording where it means a session close, so the evaluator requires a RESET_STREAM on the subscribe stream with no SUBSCRIBE_OK and no Group stream for it. Any stream code is accepted because the stream error table has no protocol-violation code. A session close instead of the reset is a Fail (the reason recorded in the evidence), and an unrelated close or no reaction does not satisfy it.

requirements.summary: A publisher does not send QUIC datagrams on the Qmux bindings (3 and 4).
requirements.rationale: The obligation binds a publisher, but only on bindings 3 and 4; the L1 runner accepts only bare QUIC and WebTransport (bindings 1 and 2), where datagrams are allowed, so the condition never arises in a run.

requirements.summary: When one endpoint closes the send direction of a bidirectional stream, the peer also closes its send direction.
requirements.rationale: The publisher is the peer when the runner ends a transaction: the runner opens an ANNOUNCE_REQUEST and a SUBSCRIBE stream, then closes its send direction with FIN, and observes that the publisher closes its own send direction (FIN or RESET_STREAM). The draft sets no deadline, so the evaluator states a generous time allowance (seconds, not a round-trip estimate) and records it in the evidence; a Fail means "not closed within the stated allowance" and says so, and a session close is not a substitute. The runner must itself close its send direction whenever the publisher closes one.

requirements.summary: After resetting the send direction of a stream, an endpoint may also close its receive direction with STOP_SENDING.
requirements.rationale: A permission: a publisher that resets without STOP_SENDING, or with it, is conforming, so there is nothing to fail. Closing the other direction remains the peer's duty under L06-4-3-MUST-025.

requirements.summary: An endpoint takes a termination code from the space matching what it terminates: session codes for a session close, stream codes for RESET_STREAM and STOP_SENDING.
requirements.rationale: The runner provokes a stream refusal (SUBSCRIBE to a broadcast the publisher does not serve) and a session termination (a malformed control message) and checks each code the publisher sends: a RESET_STREAM or STOP_SENDING code must not be one registered only in the session table (Table 2), and a session close code must not be one registered only in the stream table (Table 3). Values present in both tables cannot show the space and are accepted; unregistered values are not judged here. If either provocation produces no code (for example no session close), the evaluator reports NotRun for that half and never Pass on the other half alone. The session half also takes evidence from the session closes provoked by the MUST-level probes (l06-setup-duplicate-stream, l06-setup-duplicate-parameter, l06-setup-server-path, l06-setup-server-role, for L06-6-3-1-MUST-092, L06-7-3-MUST-112, L06-7-3-2-MUST-126 and L06-7-3-3-MUST-131), so it is not tied to the SHOULD-level reaction of L06-7-1-SHOULD-107; any one close code from those scenarios suffices for the half, and each is judged for its space only.

requirements.summary: An endpoint bridging moq-lite and MoQ Transport translates error codes according to the negotiated version and code space.
requirements.rationale: The obligation binds a protocol bridge; the publisher under test speaks moq-lite natively to the runner and bridges nothing.

requirements.summary: An endpoint does not give any error code below 32 a moq-lite-specific meaning.
requirements.rationale: The meaning an implementation attaches to a code is internal. A sub-32 code outside the moq-lite tables could still be a shared MoQ Transport code, so the wire value alone does not show a moq-lite-specific assignment; the observable part, codes drawn from the matching registered space, is judged under L06-4-4-MUST-027.

requirements.summary: An endpoint treats an error code it does not recognize as an unspecified error and otherwise ignores it.
requirements.rationale: The publisher receives codes when the runner cancels: the runner ends one of two live subscriptions with RESET_STREAM and STOP_SENDING carrying an unregistered application code (64 or above). The evaluator requires the end of that subscription to be observed (the publisher closes its send direction with FIN or RESET_STREAM, per L06-4-3-MUST-025), so a publisher that ignores the cancel cannot pass, while the session and the other subscription keep working; a session close with any code other than UNAUTHORIZED, or a refusal of later requests, is a Fail. A session close with UNAUTHORIZED (session code 0x2) after the cancel is not judged here: it is left to L06-4-4-MUST-NOT-032, so one defect never fails both rows.

requirements.summary: An endpoint does not infer a meaning for an unregistered error code.
requirements.rationale: Inference is internal. Its only observable consequences are the ones judged elsewhere: reacting to an unregistered code as more than an unspecified error (L06-4-4-MUST-030) or as an authorization failure (L06-4-4-MUST-NOT-032). Scoring this row from the same probe evidence would credit or debit a third required row for one observation.

requirements.summary: An endpoint does not treat an error code as an authorization failure unless the code is UNAUTHORIZED.
requirements.rationale: In the unknown-code probe the runner cancels a subscription with an unregistered code; the evaluator requires the end of that subscription to be observed (publisher FIN or RESET_STREAM) and then fails only a session close with UNAUTHORIZED (session code 0x2). A refusal with any other code, or stream code 0x2 (DELIVERY_TIMEOUT), is not an authorization inference and is left to L06-4-4-MUST-030. L06-4-4-MUST-030 excludes this UNAUTHORIZED session close from its own Fail, so one defect never fails both rows.

requirements.summary: An endpoint does not interpret an error code in the reserved range 32 through 47.
requirements.rationale: A distinct stimulus: the runner cancels one of two live subscriptions with RESET_STREAM and STOP_SENDING carrying a reserved code (32 through 47). The evaluator requires the end of that subscription to be observed (publisher FIN or RESET_STREAM) and the session and the other subscription to keep working; any reaction that gives the reserved value a meaning (a session close or refused later requests) is a Fail.

requirements.summary: An endpoint speaking both moq-lite and MoQ Transport maps a moq-lite code in 48-63 to the MoQ Transport code with the same meaning instead of forwarding the value.
requirements.rationale: The obligation binds an endpoint bridging both protocols; the publisher under test speaks moq-lite natively to the runner and forwards no codes to MoQ Transport.

requirements.summary: An endpoint speaking both moq-lite and MoQ Transport maps a moq-lite code in 48-63 without a MoQ Transport equivalent to an unspecified error.
requirements.rationale: The obligation binds an endpoint bridging both protocols; the publisher under test speaks moq-lite natively to the runner and forwards no codes to MoQ Transport.

requirements.summary: An endpoint that terminates a stream because its session is ending should reset it with SESSION_CLOSED rather than with the session's close code.
requirements.rationale: In L1 the runner has no stimulus that makes the publisher end its session while streams are open (GOAWAY is out of scope), and a connection close ends every stream without per-stream reset codes, so the publisher's choice is not reliably observable. The runner must itself use SESSION_CLOSED when it resets streams while closing a session.

requirements.summary: A subscriber closes the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when it receives an ANNOUNCE_END or ANNOUNCE_UPDATE naming an unassigned or retired Announce ID, an ANNOUNCE_START for an already advertised route, or any announcement before ANNOUNCE_OK.
requirements.rationale: The obligation is on the subscriber receiving announcements; the runner plays the subscriber, so it does not apply to the publisher under test. The runner must itself comply: on any of these conditions it records the offending message as evidence and closes the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (session 0x3). The publisher-side counterparts (ANNOUNCE_OK first and exactly once, a retired id never referenced again) are the section 7.5 and 7.7 rows, classified with section 7.

requirements.summary: When an Announce Stream closes, the subscriber treats every route learned on it as unavailable.
requirements.rationale: The obligation is on the subscriber's route state; the runner plays the subscriber. The runner must itself comply: after an Announce Stream ends (FIN or reset) it does not subscribe on the strength of routes learned only on that stream.

requirements.summary: Several Announce Streams, possibly with overlapping prefixes, may be open at once, each answered with its own ANNOUNCE_OK and announcements.
requirements.rationale: The permission is the subscriber's: it may open several Announce Streams with overlapping prefixes; the runner plays the subscriber. The publisher's duty to answer each with its own ANNOUNCE_OK and matching announcements is the section 7.4 MUST (draft 1755, L06-7-4-MUST-139), classified with section 7, which L1d may exercise with two overlapping ANNOUNCE_REQUESTs.

requirements.summary: A receiver discards an announcement whose reconstructed path contains its own Hop ID.
requirements.rationale: The receiver of announcements is the subscriber side of an Announce Stream; the runner plays it and the publisher under test receives no announcements in L1 (the runner serves no Announce Stream and announces nothing). The runner must itself comply: an announcement whose path contains the runner's declared Hop ID is discarded (not used for a subscription) and recorded as evidence.

requirements.summary: A receiver may close the session with a protocol violation instead of discarding a looped announcement.
requirements.rationale: A permission for the receiver of announcements, the role the runner plays; nothing applies to the publisher under test. The runner uses the discard alternative (L06-5-1-1-1-MUST-040) so a run continues after such an announcement and the evidence keeps it.

requirements.summary: A receiver may assign its own local identity to a peer that declared Hop ID 0, as selection state for that session.
requirements.rationale: Here "receiver" means the publisher, which receives the runner's SETUP Hop declaration (in L06-5-1-1-1-MUST-040 and MAY-041 the receiver of announcements is the runner). The publisher may hold such local state; it is a permission and internal, so there is nothing observable to fail.

requirements.summary: A receiver does not forward a locally assigned peer identity as a Hop ID.
requirements.rationale: Forwarding an identity means writing it into announcements sent onward to other peers, which is relay behaviour. The runner announces nothing to the publisher, so the publisher has no announcement received from the runner to forward, and anything it forwards elsewhere is not visible to the runner. The runner must itself comply: it forwards nothing.

requirements.summary: A publisher does not advertise a path whose entries contain the Hop ID the subscriber declared in its SETUP.
requirements.rationale: A publisher alone can violate it, so it is Applicable. The provocation is a known path with an entry equal to the Hop ID the runner declared in its SETUP; against an origin publisher every reconstructed path is [the publisher's own ANNOUNCE_OK Hop ID]. Not testable in L1, but not impossible: the probe is conditional on a publisher whose Hop ID is stable across sessions (draft 1719-1722 lets an endpoint declare any identity; 1782-1783 only says a fresh random value per session suffices). Session 1 reads ANNOUNCE_OK.Hop ID; session 2 declares that value in the runner's SETUP Hop Parameter, a named deliberate loop probe like L06-6-3-1-MUST-092 (the runner declares another endpoint's identity). The moq CLI, the only known target, uses a per-session random Hop ID, so the probe would be NotRun against it; it is recorded as an optional L1d/L2 item. Evidence for this row would be the announcements on an Announce Stream of session 2: Pass when no ANNOUNCE_START advertises the looped route (every reconstructed path contains the declared Hop ID).

requirements.summary: Among the paths not containing the subscriber's Hop ID a publisher advertises the best one, and advertises nothing when every known path contains it.
requirements.rationale: A publisher obligation. Choosing the best among several qualifying paths needs several upstream paths (a relay); an origin has one, so in L1 only the second half (advertise nothing when every known path contains the subscriber's Hop ID) could arise, and only through the stable-Hop-ID loop probe. Not testable in L1, but not impossible: the probe is conditional on a publisher whose Hop ID is stable across sessions (draft 1719-1722 lets an endpoint declare any identity; 1782-1783 only says a fresh random value per session suffices). Session 1 reads ANNOUNCE_OK.Hop ID; session 2 declares that value in the runner's SETUP Hop Parameter, a named deliberate loop probe like L06-6-3-1-MUST-092 (the runner declares another endpoint's identity). The moq CLI, the only known target, uses a per-session random Hop ID, so the probe would be NotRun against it; it is recorded as an optional L1d/L2 item. Evidence for this row would be the same session-2 Announce Stream: Pass when the publisher advertises nothing for the route whose only path contains the declared Hop ID (ANNOUNCE_OK with no ANNOUNCE_START for it); it shares that probe with L06-5-1-1-1-MUST-NOT-044, so L1d gives it its own evaluator or leaves it unscored rather than scoring one observation twice.

requirements.summary: When serving a subscription a publisher selects its source by the same Hop ID exclusion, and treats the subscription as unroutable when only excluded sources remain.
requirements.rationale: Applicable because an origin publisher could still violate it (serving a subscription whose only source path carries the subscriber's Hop ID); selection between several sources is relay routing. Not testable in L1, but not impossible: the probe is conditional on a publisher whose Hop ID is stable across sessions (draft 1719-1722 lets an endpoint declare any identity; 1782-1783 only says a fresh random value per session suffices). Session 1 reads ANNOUNCE_OK.Hop ID; session 2 declares that value in the runner's SETUP Hop Parameter, a named deliberate loop probe like L06-6-3-1-MUST-092 (the runner declares another endpoint's identity). The moq CLI, the only known target, uses a per-session random Hop ID, so the probe would be NotRun against it; it is recorded as an optional L1d/L2 item. Evidence for this row is different from the announcement rows: in session 2 the runner SUBSCRIBEs to the broadcast path it learned in session 1, and Pass is a refusal of that subscription (a reset of the Subscribe Stream with no SUBSCRIBE_OK and no Group stream), since the only source is excluded and the subscription is unroutable.

requirements.summary: When several routes cover a path the subscriber prefers the most specific one, then a path without a 0 Hop ID, then the lowest Warm Route Cost, then the lowest Cold Route Cost, the shortest path and the most recent.
requirements.rationale: Route resolution on the subscriber (or a relay acting as one); the runner plays the subscriber and resolves against the single publisher under test. The runner must itself comply: when several announced routes cover the path it subscribes to, it picks by this order (in practice the exact broadcast path).

requirements.summary: A relay may move a live subscription between routes with the same non-zero first hop, resuming at a group boundary.
requirements.rationale: A routing decision made by a relay; the implementation under test is an origin publisher whose session ends at the runner.

requirements.summary: A relay does not splice a live subscription across routes with differing or unknown (0) first hops.
requirements.rationale: A routing decision made by a relay between upstream routes; the implementation under test is an origin publisher with no upstream route to splice.

requirements.summary: A relay does not announce a concrete path merely because it resolved a request for it through a covering route.
requirements.rationale: A relay routing obligation (resolving a request against upstream covering routes); the implementation under test is an origin publisher.

requirements.summary: An advertiser of a covering route announces the concrete path once it is producing that broadcast.
requirements.rationale: The advertiser can be an origin publisher, so it is Applicable, but it needs a publisher that advertises a covering route and starts producing on demand. The L1 target (the moq CLI) publishes one concrete broadcast path and no stimulus makes it advertise a covering route, so the condition does not arise.

requirements.summary: A deployment relying on standby ordering bounds the number of charged links on an admitted path by H and each charged link cost by C.
requirements.rationale: A deployment-wide configuration obligation across relays and links, not wire behaviour of a single publisher; the runner cannot see whether a deployment relies on standby ordering or what its bounds are.

requirements.summary: A deployment relying on standby ordering enforces its H and C bounds when admitting paths and links.
requirements.rationale: Admission of paths and links is done by relays of the deployment, not by an origin publisher on its session with the runner.

requirements.summary: In a deployment relying on standby ordering, an origin already producing a broadcast seeds its route cost at 0.
requirements.rationale: An origin publisher can violate it, so it is Applicable, but the obligation binds only deployments relying on standby ordering and the runner cannot know whether the publisher is in one; outside such a deployment a non-zero seed is legal. A non-zero Warm or Cold cost on an origin's ANNOUNCE_START is therefore not a violation the runner can establish. L1d announce evaluators may record the costs as information only.

requirements.summary: In a deployment relying on standby ordering, a standby origin seeds its cost with S where H * C < S < the saturation ceiling.
requirements.rationale: Binds a standby origin (one that would start producing on demand) in a deployment whose H and C the runner cannot know; the L1 target is an already-producing origin, so the condition does not arise.

requirements.summary: A standby origin uses a seed of 2^32 only when H * C < 2^32.
requirements.rationale: Same condition as L06-5-1-1-2-MUST-055: a standby origin in a deployment with bounds unknown to the runner; the L1 target is not a standby origin.

requirements.summary: A receiver resolving routes does not assume that unknown, out-of-budget or saturated routes outrank standby capacity.
requirements.rationale: Route selection by the endpoint resolving a request across routes (a relay, or a subscriber); the publisher under test resolves nothing across upstream routes. The runner must itself comply: it does not prefer such a route because it might already carry content.

requirements.summary: A receiver that has spent its one re-resolution after NO_CAPACITY, or has nothing to re-resolve to, resets the downstream request with a code other than NO_CAPACITY.
requirements.rationale: The receiver here holds a downstream request it resolved towards an upstream advertiser, which is a relay; an origin publisher has no upstream to retry and the runner has no downstream. Its own refusals are judged by L06-5-1-2-MUST-062 and the code-space row L06-4-4-MUST-027.

requirements.summary: A receiver resolving requests does not cache refusals.
requirements.rationale: The receiver is the endpoint resolving requests against upstream advertisers (a relay); the origin publisher under test refuses but does not resolve. The runner must itself comply: it does not cache a refusal across scenarios and every scenario sends its requests afresh.

requirements.summary: A subscriber starts a Subscribe Stream with one SUBSCRIBE message, optionally followed by SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE messages.
requirements.rationale: Constrains what the subscriber writes; the runner plays the subscriber. The runner must itself comply on every Subscribe Stream (STREAM_TYPE then SUBSCRIBE first); only a framing probe named as a deliberate violation in L1d's errors scenarios may send anything else first.

requirements.summary: For a live track a publisher may withhold SUBSCRIBE_OK until the first matching group resolves the start, and answers a track already ended with no matching group with SUBSCRIBE_END and no SUBSCRIBE_OK.
requirements.rationale: A permission, so nothing to fail. L1d subscribe evaluators must accept a SUBSCRIBE_OK that arrives only with or after the first matching group (within their stated allowances), and a SUBSCRIBE_END without SUBSCRIBE_OK for an ended track. The non-keyword sentence about SUBSCRIBE_END with no preceding SUBSCRIBE_OK is used only as tolerance guidance for evaluators, not judged as a row.

requirements.summary: A publisher that cannot serve a subscription (no such track, an ended broadcast, a covered path naming nothing, or any other refusal) promptly resets the Subscribe Stream instead of leaving it pending.
requirements.rationale: After an announce exchange the runner opens two Subscribe Streams, each with a conforming SUBSCRIBE: (a) a broadcast path that no route the publisher announced covers (outside every announced prefix), which the publisher cannot serve, and (b) a track name the announced broadcast does not serve. The draft says "reset the stream", so per stream the evaluator requires a RESET_STREAM from the publisher on the subscribe stream, with no SUBSCRIBE_OK and no Group stream for that Subscribe ID; any code is accepted here (the code space is L06-4-4-MUST-027). The draft gives no deadline for "promptly", so the evaluator uses a generous stated allowance (a few seconds, recorded in the evidence). For case (a) a stream still pending at the end of the allowance is a Fail, flagged as time-bounded ("not reset within the allowance"). For case (b) a pending stream is NotRun, not Fail: for a live track the publisher MAY withhold SUBSCRIBE_OK until a matching group resolves the start (draft 1038-1039), and the runner cannot prove the track will never exist. In both cases a SUBSCRIBE_END or FIN instead of a reset, or a session close instead of the stream reset, is a Fail with the reason recorded.

requirements.summary: A subscriber may open the Track and Subscribe streams concurrently, buffering frames until TRACK_INFO arrives.
requirements.rationale: A permission for the subscriber; the runner plays it. Track streams are L2, so the L1 runner decodes FRAMEs without TRACK_INFO and does not interpret timestamps against a timescale.

requirements.summary: A publisher may close the Subscribe Stream with FIN after SUBSCRIBE_END, once stragglers in the range are dropped or delivered.
requirements.rationale: A permission, nothing to fail. L1d subscribe evaluators must accept SUBSCRIBE_DROP and Group streams for groups within the range after SUBSCRIBE_END and a FIN only after that.

requirements.summary: Either endpoint may reset a Subscribe Stream at any time.
requirements.rationale: A permission for both sides, nothing to fail. L1d evaluators that need groups from a served subscription must report an early publisher reset of it as inconclusive (NotRun), not as a Fail, unless the row they judge forbids it; the runner uses its own permission to cancel subscriptions (the L06-4-4-MUST-030 probe).

requirements.summary: A publisher that cannot serve the requested frame range in full resets the Fetch Stream rather than return a shorter run.
requirements.rationale: The publisher half of the reset-not-truncate rule is judged on the one request it can never serve: a FETCH for a group sequence far beyond anything the track has produced. The reply has no header, so the only conforming outcome is a RESET_STREAM on the Fetch Stream; any stream code is accepted because the draft names none for this case (NOT_FOUND 0x33 is the natural one). A FIN, with or without frames, is a Fail: an empty or short run is exactly the truncation the draft forbids. A publisher that did not reply before the observation window ended is NotRun, never a Pass. The rule is judged on this unservable request alone; L06-7-16-MUST-177 is judged on requests for groups the publisher does hold, so one defect never fails both rows.

requirements.summary: The subscriber must already have the track's TRACK_INFO to parse the frames a FETCH returns.
requirements.rationale: A subscriber duty: the runner plays the subscriber. The runner opens a Track Stream for the track and keeps the TRACK_INFO before it FETCHes or reads frames on that track. Its FETCH scenarios send TRACK first and read the response only against that TRACK_INFO. The same duty is restated in section 7.16 (L06-7-16-MUST-176).

requirements.summary: A subscriber should cache TRACK_INFO by broadcast path and track name and reuse it across SUBSCRIBE and FETCH.
requirements.rationale: A subscriber duty: the runner plays the subscriber. Each scenario context opens one Track Stream per track and reuses its TRACK_INFO for every later SUBSCRIBE and FETCH on that track within the context. The publisher side of the same paragraph (immutability) is L06-7-12-MUST-NOT-163.

requirements.summary: A subscriber that cannot decode FRAMEs against the cached TRACK_INFO resets the affected stream with a protocol violation and re-requests it.
requirements.rationale: A subscriber duty: the runner plays the subscriber for probing only. It is a passive recorder: bytes that do not decode are kept as decode issues on the stream record and judged by the evaluators, and the runner does not run a subscriber's recovery (reset and re-request). No planned scenario depends on it. Recorded as a known runner gap in docs/interop-notes.md.

requirements.summary: A publisher should prioritize TRACK_INFO ahead of group data on the connection.
requirements.rationale: A transmission-order preference inside the publisher's QUIC send scheduler. The runner sees the order bytes arrive on different streams, which also reflects network reordering and its own read order, so any verdict would rest on a timing guess. No scenario is planned.

requirements.summary: The subscriber may send additional PROBE messages on the same stream to update the target bitrate.
requirements.rationale: The permission is the subscriber's: the runner may send several targets on one Probe Stream and the l06-probe-report scenario does. The publisher's duty to treat each one as a new target is L06-5-1-5-MUST-072.

requirements.summary: The publisher treats each PROBE message from the subscriber as a new target to attempt and keeps the stream open.
requirements.rationale: Judged only for a publisher that advertised Probe level Report or Increase in its SETUP (draft 7.3.1; the evaluator reads the level from the publisher's decoded SETUP). The runner opens a Probe Stream, sends one target, waits for a report, then sends a second, different target. Treating a target as a new target to attempt means the stream stays usable: a Report-level publisher ignores the value and keeps reporting, an Increase-level publisher pads. The observable is therefore that neither target resets the stream or closes the session and that the publisher's reports continue after the second target. A RESET_STREAM of the Probe Stream after a target is a Fail (the moq CLI resets with MALFORMED_TRACK on any runner target message, candidate defect P1). A publisher that never reported before the second target, or advertised level None (the stream reset is then L06-5-1-5-MUST-075), is NotRun. The padding itself is not observed (L06-5-1-5-SHOULD-073).

requirements.summary: A publisher that advertised Increase should pad the connection to reach the most recent target bitrate without exceeding the congestion window.
requirements.rationale: Padding is only visible as sustained throughput above the publisher's media rate, which depends on the congestion controller, the path and the media source; a SHOULD about reaching a target cannot be failed from the stream layer. The moq CLI also advertises no Increase level to pad with. No scenario is planned.

requirements.summary: A publisher that advertised Report but not Increase must not pad above its current sending rate.
requirements.rationale: Needs a measurement of the publisher's sending rate against the target over time, separated from its media rate and from congestion control. The runner has no calibrated throughput meter, so a Pass would be a guess and a Fail unreliable. No scenario is planned.

requirements.summary: A publisher that advertised no Probe capability resets the Probe Stream.
requirements.rationale: Judged only for a publisher whose decoded SETUP carries no Probe parameter or Level 0 (the draft makes the two equivalent, 7.3.1). The runner opens a Probe Stream and sends a target; the publisher must RESET_STREAM it (any code: the draft names none). A PROBE report answered instead of a reset is a Fail (the moq CLI answers at level None, candidate defect P2). A publisher that advertised Report or Increase is NotRun for this row (its stream is judged by L06-5-1-5-MUST-072), as is one that neither answered nor reset inside the observation window. The runner never reads a missing SETUP as level None: with no decoded SETUP the row is NotRun.

requirements.summary: The peer that receives a GOAWAY with a non-empty URI should establish a new session at that URI and migrate its active subscriptions.
requirements.rationale: Whether a publisher application reconnects is an application policy and needs a second listener the runner can recognize as the redirect target, plus an observation window of several seconds; a SHOULD that an application may reasonably decline cannot be failed. The runner's GOAWAY URI in l06-goaway-single is a non-routable name on purpose, so no peer dials it. Left for L2b.

requirements.summary: The peer that receives a GOAWAY must not open new streams on the current session.
requirements.rationale: The runner subscribes, waits until the publisher has opened at least three Group streams (the first is usually the group already in progress, so only the gaps from the second stream on measure a whole group interval; the observation after the allowance must outlast the longest of them) of its own accord (the proof that it opens streams on a regular cadence), then sends a GOAWAY and watches. The rule binds the receiver of the GOAWAY, and a stream the publisher opened before it saw the GOAWAY may still arrive, so a stated allowance of 2000 ms after the GOAWAY was written covers that flight time: a publisher-opened stream whose first byte arrives after the allowance is a Fail; streams that existed before the GOAWAY keep being served and are not judged (the draft lets the sender close the stream when it is ready). Without the pre-GOAWAY cadence proof, with a publisher that closed the session, or with the GOAWAY not delivered, the row is NotRun: no new stream after a GOAWAY proves nothing for a publisher that was not opening streams anyway.

requirements.summary: The peer should close all streams and the session after migrating or when it no longer needs the session.
requirements.rationale: Depends on when the application decides it no longer needs the session, which the draft gives no time for; an absent close inside any window the runner picks proves nothing. No scenario is planned.

requirements.summary: Each endpoint opens a Setup Stream (stream type 0x1) at the start of the session to advertise its optional capabilities and extensions.
requirements.rationale: Restates L06-3-1-MUST-014, which is Testable through l06-setup-stream / l06-setup-stream-single-setup (one unidirectional stream with the Setup STREAM_TYPE 0x1, one SETUP, FIN). The same observation would judge this row, so it is not scored separately to avoid crediting or debiting two required rows with one piece of evidence. The runner must itself open its own Setup Stream.

requirements.summary: An endpoint that receives a second Setup Stream closes the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.rationale: A named deliberate violation probe: after its first Setup Stream has been sent and finished, the runner opens a second unidirectional Setup Stream (STREAM_TYPE 0x1, an empty SETUP, FIN), which breaks "exactly one Setup Stream per direction", and sends nothing else. The draft says "close the session", so the evaluator requires a session close with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (session code 0x3) observed by the runner; a reset or STOP_SENDING of the second stream alone, a close with another code, or a session still open at the end of a generous stated allowance (the draft gives no deadline; a few seconds, recorded in the evidence) is a Fail, the last one flagged as time-bounded. The runner must itself comply when the publisher opens a second Setup Stream.

requirements.summary: A Group Stream starts with a GROUP message.
requirements.rationale: The runner announces, then subscribes to an announced track with a default SUBSCRIBE (latest group, unbounded) and observes Group streams for a stated window long enough to see at least two groups of the target's group cadence (recorded in the evidence; the same window serves L06-6-3-2-MUST-NOT-097). For every unidirectional stream with STREAM_TYPE Group (0x0) the evaluator decodes the first message with the L1b codec and requires a GROUP before any FRAME. A Group stream reset before any byte after STREAM_TYPE is skipped, not failed (either side MAY reset a Group stream). Checking that the GROUP's Subscribe ID names the open subscription is an extension beyond the bare wording and is recorded as information, not judged by this row. If no Group stream arrives within the window the row is NotRun (the publisher may legitimately reset a subscription), never a Pass.

requirements.summary: A GROUP message may be followed by any number of FRAME messages.
requirements.rationale: A permission, nothing to fail; group evaluators accept any number of FRAMEs after the GROUP.

requirements.summary: A group may contain zero FRAME messages, for example to signal a gap in the track.
requirements.rationale: A permission, nothing to fail; group evaluators accept a Group stream that ends (FIN) right after its GROUP.

requirements.summary: A FRAME may carry an empty payload, for example to signal a gap in the group.
requirements.rationale: A permission, nothing to fail; frame evaluators accept a zero-length payload.

requirements.summary: A publisher does not send two Group Streams for the same Group Sequence on one subscription.
requirements.rationale: Judged on the same default subscription as L06-6-3-2-MUST-093 but on a different property: across every Group stream carrying the subscription's Subscribe ID (completed or reset after its GROUP decoded) no Group Sequence appears twice. The observation window is the one stated for 093, long enough to see at least two groups. A Group stream reset before its GROUP decoded is skipped, not failed. The runner sends no SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE in this scenario, so nothing it does invites a resend. A violation needs at least two Group streams, so with fewer than two decoded in the window the row is NotRun, not Pass.

requirements.summary: Either the publisher or the subscriber may reset a Group Stream at any time, without ending the session.
requirements.rationale: A permission, nothing to fail. The runner must not treat a reset Group stream as fatal (the draft says the session remains active), and group evaluators count a reset Group stream as accounted for.

requirements.summary: A subscriber may cache a Group stream error and retry later.
requirements.rationale: A permission for the subscriber; the runner plays it and does not cache errors across scenarios.
