requirements.summary: An endpoint that receives a message whose Message Length does not match its fields closes the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.rationale: The publisher is the receiver of the runner's control messages. This reuses the session half of l06-errors-code-space (L06-4-4-MUST-027), whose malformed control message L1d makes a Message Length mismatch: a well-formed ANNOUNCE_REQUEST whose Message Length covers the prefix string plus trailing bytes. 027 judges only the code space of the close (and also takes session-close evidence from the MUST-level probes of 092, 112, 126 and 131, so it does not depend on this SHOULD-level reaction); this evaluator judges a different property, attributed to this row only, that the session is closed with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (session code 0x3). The draft says "close the connection", so a stream reset or STOP_SENDING alone, a close with another code, or a session still open at the end of a generous stated allowance (no deadline is given; seconds, recorded in the evidence) is a Fail of this SHOULD row, the last flagged as time-bounded. The runner must itself close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION on a publisher message with an unexpected length (the L1b decoders report it as ProtocolViolation).

requirements.summary: A receiver resets a stream whose STREAM_TYPE it does not know.
requirements.rationale: The publisher receives the streams the runner opens. Opening an unknown stream type is anticipated by the draft (the fallback for an extension stream opened against a peer that did not negotiate it), so this is not a violation probe: after the setup exchange the runner opens a bidirectional stream whose STREAM_TYPE is an unregistered value (not 0x0-0x6; the value is recorded in the evidence) and writes nothing else. The draft says "reset the stream", so the evaluator requires the publisher to reset it: a RESET_STREAM on the publisher's send half or a STOP_SENDING on the runner's send half (the receiver's QUIC reset of that direction), whichever comes first, recorded. A FIN without a reset, or no reaction within a generous stated allowance (the draft gives no deadline; seconds, recorded), is a Fail, the latter flagged as time-bounded. A session close is judged by L06-7-2-MUST-NOT-109 only; for this row it makes the stream reset unobservable and the row NotRun, so one close never debits both rows. The runner must itself reset an unknown-type stream the publisher opens and keep the session.

requirements.summary: A receiver does not treat an unknown STREAM_TYPE as fatal to the session.
requirements.rationale: Same stimulus as L06-7-2-MUST-108, a different property: after opening the unknown-type stream the runner sends a conforming ANNOUNCE_REQUEST on a new Announce Stream. The evaluator requires the session to stay open for the stated window and the request to be answered with ANNOUNCE_OK. A session close (any code) after the unknown stream, or a refusal of the follow-up request, is a Fail. Whether the unknown stream itself was reset is not judged here (that is 108).

requirements.summary: A SETUP receiver ignores Parameter IDs it does not know.
requirements.rationale: The publisher receives the runner's SETUP. In this scenario the runner's SETUP carries, besides what it would send anyway, one parameter with an id the draft does not define (not 0x1-0x5) and that the target is not known to use, with a short value; the id is recorded in the evidence. This is conforming (the draft anticipates new capabilities). Ignoring is internal, so the evaluator judges its observable consequence: the publisher's own SETUP arrives, a following ANNOUNCE_REQUEST is answered with ANNOUNCE_OK, and the session stays open for the stated window. A session close (any code) or a refusal of the request is a Fail. The runner must itself ignore unknown Parameter IDs in the publisher's SETUP (read_capabilities does).

requirements.summary: A SETUP message does not carry the same Parameter ID more than once.
requirements.rationale: Observable by decoding the publisher's SETUP on every session with the L1b codec (decode_setup reports a repeated id as ProtocolViolation). This is a different property from L06-3-1-MUST-014 (one SETUP on one Setup stream ending with FIN): L1d's 014 evaluator must treat a SETUP whose framing is intact but whose only defect is a repeated id as a decoded SETUP, so one defect debits only this row. A Parameter ID appearing twice is a Fail. A duplicate needs at least two parameters, so with fewer than two the row is NotRun rather than a vacuous Pass. The runner must itself never repeat a Parameter ID except in the named probe of L06-7-3-MUST-112, whose raw SETUP bytes L1d builds with write_framed_message and the field writers because encode_setup refuses duplicate ids.

requirements.summary: A receiver closes the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when a SETUP repeats a Parameter ID.
requirements.rationale: A named deliberate violation probe: the runner's SETUP carries the Cost parameter (0x4, which the runner may legally send once) twice with the same value, so the repetition is the only defect, and the runner sends nothing else that could provoke a close. The draft says "close the session", so the evaluator requires a session close with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (session code 0x3); a stream-level reaction alone (reset or STOP_SENDING of the runner's Setup stream), a close with another code, or a session still open at the end of a generous stated allowance (seconds, recorded) is a Fail, the last flagged as time-bounded. The runner must itself close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when the publisher's SETUP repeats an id. encode_setup refuses duplicate ids, so L1d builds this probe's raw SETUP bytes with write_framed_message and the field writers.

requirements.summary: A subscriber consults the publisher's advertised Probe level before relying on a Probe Stream.
requirements.rationale: Binds the subscriber; the runner plays it. The runner must itself comply: Probe Streams are out of the L1 scope (design spec: L2), so the L1 runner opens none and records the publisher's Probe level only.

requirements.summary: A subscriber does not open a Probe Stream to a publisher whose Probe level is None.
requirements.rationale: Binds the subscriber; the runner plays it and opens no Probe Stream in L1.

requirements.summary: A publisher at Probe level None resets any Probe Stream a subscriber opens.
requirements.rationale: A publisher obligation, but Probe Streams are out of the L1 scope (design spec: Probe, Fetch, Goaway and Track streams are L2). The provocation is itself a deviation (the subscriber SHOULD NOT open one at None) and only arises against a publisher that advertises None or omits the parameter. L2 can test it with a named probe that opens a Probe Stream (0x4) and requires a reset of that stream; the evaluator would be NotRun against a publisher advertising Report or Increase.

requirements.summary: At Probe level Report a subscriber may open a Probe Stream to monitor the estimated bitrate.
requirements.rationale: A permission of the subscriber; the runner plays it and opens no Probe Stream in L1.

requirements.summary: At Probe level Report a subscriber does not expect the publisher to pad above its current sending rate.
requirements.rationale: Binds the subscriber's expectations; the runner plays it and opens no Probe Stream in L1.

requirements.summary: A subscriber that needs to probe for more bandwidth from a Report-level publisher uses an alternative such as switching to a higher rendition.
requirements.rationale: Binds the subscriber; the runner plays it and does no bandwidth probing in L1.

requirements.summary: At Probe level Increase a subscriber may request a target bitrate and expect the publisher to probe up to it.
requirements.rationale: A permission of the subscriber; the runner plays it and opens no Probe Stream in L1.

requirements.summary: When the session URI carries a query, the client's Path parameter value is the URI path followed by ? and the query component.
requirements.rationale: In L1 the publisher under test (the moq CLI) dials the runner, so the publisher is the CLIENT and the runner is the SERVER and the subscriber. In l06-setup-client-path the runner (through the adapter) gives the publisher a session URL with a non-empty path and a harmless query component (both recorded in the evidence); L1d runs the scenario on both bindings. On binding 1 (raw QUIC, no request URI), when the publisher's SETUP carries a Path parameter, the evaluator requires its value to equal the path-abempty component followed by ? and the query; a value without the query, or with a different one, is a Fail. A missing Path parameter is judged by L06-7-3-2-SHOULD-124 and makes this row NotRun, as do binding 2 sessions (no Path is sent there) and an adapter that cannot pass a query to the publisher.

requirements.summary: The Path value may be empty, which is equivalent to omitting it and requests the server's default path.
requirements.rationale: In L1 the publisher under test (the moq CLI) dials the runner, so the publisher is the CLIENT and the runner is the SERVER and the subscriber. A permission of the client (the publisher) with nothing to fail. The runner, as server, must itself treat an empty Path exactly like an absent one, and the l06-setup-client-path evaluators must accept it as such.

requirements.summary: A server that receives an invalid Path value closes the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.rationale: In L1 the publisher under test (the moq CLI) dials the runner, so the publisher is the CLIENT and the runner is the SERVER and the subscriber. This binds the server, which is the runner. The runner must itself comply, but the interpretation of Path is application-defined and opaque to moq-lite (draft 1634-1635), so the runner treats only a value that is not a path-abempty with an optional ? and query as invalid, and records it. A publisher Path defect stays attributable to L06-7-3-2-MUST-120 in l06-setup-client-path and is not turned into a session close in every scenario: in other scenarios the runner records the value and continues. On a URI binding where the publisher sends a Path parameter, the runner records the value and continues in every session so the defect is attributed to L06-7-3-2-MUST-120 or L06-7-3-2-MUST-NOT-125; the runner closes with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION only on the dedicated l06-setup-server-path probe session.

requirements.summary: A server that does not recognize the requested Path closes the session.
requirements.rationale: In L1 the publisher under test (the moq CLI) dials the runner, so the publisher is the CLIENT and the runner is the SERVER and the subscriber. This binds the server, which is the runner. Path interpretation is application-defined (draft 1634-1635) and the runner serves a single test endpoint, so it recognizes any path (absent and empty included) and records the received value; it never closes on an unrecognized path, which keeps a publisher Path defect attributable to L06-7-3-2-MUST-120 rather than ending every scenario. On a URI binding where the publisher sends a Path parameter, the runner records the value and continues in every session so the defect is attributed to L06-7-3-2-MUST-120 or L06-7-3-2-MUST-NOT-125; the runner closes with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION only on the dedicated l06-setup-server-path probe session.

requirements.summary: A client on a binding without a request URI (bindings 1 and 3) sends the Path parameter.
requirements.rationale: In L1 the publisher under test (the moq CLI) dials the runner, so the publisher is the CLIENT and the runner is the SERVER and the subscriber. Judged on the binding 1 (raw QUIC) sessions of l06-setup-client-path from the publisher's decoded SETUP: a Path parameter present (an empty value counts as sent) is a Pass and an absent one a Fail of this SHOULD row. Binding 2 sessions make the row NotRun. The value's format is judged separately by L06-7-3-2-MUST-120.

requirements.summary: The Path parameter is not sent on a binding whose handshake carries a request URI (bindings 2 and 4).
requirements.rationale: In L1 the publisher under test (the moq CLI) dials the runner, so the publisher is the CLIENT and the runner is the SERVER and the subscriber. Judged on the binding 2 (WebTransport) sessions of l06-setup-client-path from the publisher's decoded SETUP: a Path parameter (any value, empty included) is a Fail; no Path is a Pass. Binding 1 sessions make the row NotRun. The runner listens only on bindings 1 and 2, so binding 4 never arises.

requirements.summary: A receiver closes the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when the Path parameter is sent on a URI binding or by the server.
requirements.rationale: In L1 the publisher under test (the moq CLI) dials the runner, so the publisher is the CLIENT and the runner is the SERVER and the subscriber. The sentence has two halves. A Path on a URI binding is received by the server (the runner), which must itself close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION and record it, but only on the dedicated l06-setup-server-path probe session; in every other session the runner records the value and continues so the defect is attributed to L06-7-3-2-MUST-NOT-125 and L06-7-3-2-MUST-120. A Path sent by the server is received by the client, the publisher, so that half is tested with a named deliberate violation probe: on binding 1, so that only the "only the client sends it" rule is broken, the runner's SETUP carries a Path parameter (a plain value such as "/"). The evaluator requires a session close with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (session code 0x3); a stream-level reaction alone, a close with another code, or a session still open at the end of a generous stated allowance (seconds, recorded) is a Fail, the last flagged as time-bounded.

requirements.summary: A relay does not forward the Path parameter to another hop.
requirements.rationale: Binds a relay; the publisher under test is an origin and the runner forwards nothing.

requirements.summary: A receiver of the Role parameter treats an unrecognized value as Both.
requirements.rationale: In L1 the publisher under test (the moq CLI) dials the runner, so the publisher is the CLIENT and the runner is the SERVER and the subscriber. Only the client sends Role, so its receiver is the server, which is the runner. The runner must itself comply: an unknown Role value from the publisher is treated as Both (effective_role in the L1b codec) and is not a reason to close.

requirements.summary: A server enforces the client's authorization on every publish and subscribe regardless of the advertised Role.
requirements.rationale: In L1 the publisher under test (the moq CLI) dials the runner, so the publisher is the CLIENT and the runner is the SERVER and the subscriber. Binds the server, which is the runner; the runner applies no authorization in L1 and accepts any publisher, so it never refuses on authorization grounds.

requirements.summary: A server may close a session whose advertised Role requires a direction the client's authorization does not grant.
requirements.rationale: In L1 the publisher under test (the moq CLI) dials the runner, so the publisher is the CLIENT and the runner is the SERVER and the subscriber. A permission of the server, which is the runner; the runner does not use it.

requirements.summary: A client that receives a Role parameter closes the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.rationale: In L1 the publisher under test (the moq CLI) dials the runner, so the publisher is the CLIENT and the runner is the SERVER and the subscriber. The publisher is the client, so this is testable with a named deliberate violation probe: the runner's SETUP carries a Role parameter (value 0, Both, so only the sender is wrong) and nothing else that could provoke a close. The evaluator requires a session close with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (session code 0x3); a stream-level reaction alone, a close with another code, or a session still open at the end of a generous stated allowance (seconds, recorded) is a Fail, the last flagged as time-bounded. The runner, as server, must itself never send Role outside this probe.

requirements.summary: A relay does not forward the Role parameter.
requirements.rationale: Binds a relay; the publisher under test is an origin and the runner forwards nothing.

requirements.summary: A relay does not forward the Cost parameter.
requirements.rationale: Binds a relay; the publisher under test is an origin and the runner forwards nothing.

requirements.summary: A receiver may charge a locally configured cost instead of the Cost its peer declared.
requirements.rationale: A permission of whichever endpoint receives Cost, the publisher included, with nothing to fail. The declared cost only affects announcements the declaring peer forwards, and the runner announces nothing to the publisher in L1, so its effect is not observable either.

requirements.summary: Either endpoint may send the Hop parameter declaring its Hop ID.
requirements.rationale: A permission for the publisher (and the runner) with nothing to fail. The publisher's declared value is recorded as information alongside its ANNOUNCE_OK Hop ID.

requirements.summary: A subscriber-only endpoint with no identity may omit the Hop parameter.
requirements.rationale: A permission of a subscriber-only endpoint, which is the runner's role; the publisher under test is not subscriber-only. The runner may omit it or declare a per-session Hop ID (as the optional L2 loop probe of L06-5-1-1-1-MUST-NOT-044 would).

requirements.summary: A publisher has a Hop ID even when it could omit the Hop parameter.
requirements.rationale: The publisher's identity is observable as its ANNOUNCE_OK Hop ID, which L06-7-5-SHOULD-143 judges (non-zero means assigned). Scoring this row from the same value would count one observation twice. Whether this sentence also asks for the Hop parameter in SETUP is ambiguous ("have", with a pointer to ANNOUNCE_OK), so the SETUP value is recorded as information only.

requirements.summary: A relay does not forward the Hop parameter.
requirements.rationale: Binds a relay; the publisher under test is an origin and the runner forwards nothing.

requirements.summary: A publisher answers an ANNOUNCE_REQUEST with ANNOUNCE_OK, then ANNOUNCE_START for every matching route, then ANNOUNCE_START, ANNOUNCE_END and ANNOUNCE_UPDATE for later changes.
requirements.rationale: In l06-announce-prefix the runner opens Announce Streams with an ANNOUNCE_REQUEST for the empty prefix, for a prefix of the publisher's configured broadcast path (both open at once, so two overlapping requests are exercised) and for a prefix disjoint from it, and decodes every message on the response side with the L1b codecs for a stated window (seconds, recorded in the evidence). Per stream the evaluator requires the first message to decode as ANNOUNCE_OK within a generous stated allowance (the draft gives no deadline; a missing ANNOUNCE_OK is a Fail flagged as time-bounded) and every later message to decode as ANNOUNCE_START, ANNOUNCE_END or ANNOUNCE_UPDATE. The Active Count of ANNOUNCE_OK announces the initial set, so the next Active Count messages must be ANNOUNCE_STARTs arriving within the allowance; fewer is a Fail, flagged as time-bounded, except that an ANNOUNCE_END for an id of the initial set (a route ending while the initial set is still arriving) makes the Active Count check inconclusive rather than a Fail. For the empty prefix and the broadcast's prefix an ANNOUNCE_START whose reconstructed route covers the configured broadcast path must arrive within the allowance, otherwise Fail (time-bounded). For the disjoint prefix only ANNOUNCE_OK is required; any routes there are recorded, since the runner cannot prove the publisher serves nothing under it. A session close or a reset instead of the answer is a Fail. A START or UPDATE that fails to decode, including a Hop Count mismatch or a duplicate non-zero Hop ID (the L1b decoder reports both as ProtocolViolation), is a Fail of this row with the decode error recorded; no other row is debited for it (L06-7-6-MUST-146 and L06-7-6-MUST-149 are the runner's receiver duties). The overlapping pair covers the publisher side of L06-5-1-1-MAY-039 (each stream answered on its own). An ANNOUNCE message with an unknown Type is not judged here: moq.dev skips it by Message Length while the L1b decoder returns InvalidValue, and that decision is open for the L1d session layer (handoff.from_L1b DEFERRED (b)); until it is made such a message is recorded and the stream is inconclusive for this row from that point on, never a Fail (an unknown Type stays inconclusive, not a decode failure).

requirements.summary: An implementation limits the number of matching broadcasts it tracks for an ANNOUNCE_REQUEST to prevent resource exhaustion.
requirements.rationale: A resource-limit guideline with no stated threshold, internal to the publisher. Provoking it would need the runner to drive a large number of broadcasts, which an origin publisher with one broadcast cannot show, and the runner announces nothing.

requirements.summary: ANNOUNCE_START and ANNOUNCE_UPDATE do not repeat the stream's ANNOUNCE_OK Hop ID as the last entry of their Hop ID list.
requirements.rationale: In l06-announce-prefix the runner opens Announce Streams with an ANNOUNCE_REQUEST for the empty prefix, for a prefix of the publisher's configured broadcast path (both open at once, so two overlapping requests are exercised) and for a prefix disjoint from it, and decodes every message on the response side with the L1b codecs for a stated window (seconds, recorded in the evidence). For every stream whose ANNOUNCE_OK Hop ID is non-zero, an ANNOUNCE_START or ANNOUNCE_UPDATE whose Hop ID list ends with that value is a Fail (a common bug: an origin listing itself with Hop Count 1). Pass needs at least one decoded ANNOUNCE_START or ANNOUNCE_UPDATE on such a stream. With an ANNOUNCE_OK Hop ID of 0 the row is NotRun (0 means unknown, and repeated 0 entries are legal), as it is when no ANNOUNCE_START or ANNOUNCE_UPDATE is decoded. An ANNOUNCE message with an unknown Type is not judged here: moq.dev skips it by Message Length while the L1b decoder returns InvalidValue, and that decision is open for the L1d session layer (handoff.from_L1b DEFERRED (b)); until it is made such a message is recorded and the stream is inconclusive for this row from that point on, never a Fail.

requirements.summary: A publisher that assigns itself a Hop ID chooses a non-zero value.
requirements.rationale: On the wire a Hop ID of 0 means "unknown": not assigned, or deliberately withheld, both legal. A publisher that assigned 0 is therefore indistinguishable from one that assigned nothing or withholds its identity, so no observation can show a violation. Whether the publisher has a Hop ID at all is the SHOULD of L06-7-5-SHOULD-143.

requirements.summary: A publisher assigns itself a non-zero Hop ID (a fresh random value per session suffices) so downstream receivers can detect loops.
requirements.rationale: In l06-announce-prefix the runner opens Announce Streams with an ANNOUNCE_REQUEST for the empty prefix, for a prefix of the publisher's configured broadcast path (both open at once, so two overlapping requests are exercised) and for a prefix disjoint from it, and decodes every message on the response side with the L1b codecs for a stated window (seconds, recorded in the evidence). The evaluator reads the Hop ID of each ANNOUNCE_OK: a non-zero value is a Pass, and 0 (no identity, or withheld) is a Fail of this SHOULD row. No ANNOUNCE_OK makes the row NotRun (L06-7-4-MUST-139 judges its absence). The publisher's SETUP Hop parameter is recorded alongside as information.

requirements.summary: A subscriber may hold back announcements until all Active Count initial announcements have arrived and deliver them as a batch.
requirements.rationale: A permission of the subscriber; the runner plays it. The runner does not batch for judging: it records every announcement as it arrives.

requirements.summary: A subscriber reports announcements beyond the Active Count initial set as they arrive.
requirements.rationale: Binds the subscriber's reporting to its application; the runner plays the subscriber and records live announcements as they arrive.

requirements.summary: A receiver closes the stream with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when an ANNOUNCE_START or ANNOUNCE_UPDATE carries a Hop Count that does not match the number of Hop ID entries that follow.
requirements.rationale: The close duty binds the receiver of announcements, which is the subscriber side of the Announce Stream; the runner plays it, so it does not apply to the publisher under test (the publisher receives no announcements in L1). The runner must itself comply: on a Hop Count mismatch in a publisher announcement it closes that Announce Stream with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION and records the raw message as evidence. Following the receiver-close convention of draft 22 (D22-4-2-MUST-109) and L06-5-1-1-MUST-037, this close rule is not turned into a publisher rule; a publisher announcement that fails to decode, a Hop Count mismatch included, is judged once, by L06-7-4-MUST-139.

requirements.summary: A relay forwarding an upstream announcement appends the upstream peer's ANNOUNCE_OK Hop ID to the Hop ID list.
requirements.rationale: Binds a relay forwarding announcements; the L1 publisher is an origin (its routes originate locally) and the runner forwards nothing.

requirements.summary: A relay does not forward an identity it assigned to an upstream as a Hop ID.
requirements.rationale: Binds a relay that assigns local identities to its upstreams; the L1 publisher is an origin and the runner forwards nothing.

requirements.summary: A receiver closes the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION when a non-zero Hop ID appears twice in one announcement's Hop ID list; repeated 0 entries are legal.
requirements.rationale: The close duty binds the receiver of announcements, which is the subscriber side of the Announce Stream; the runner plays it, so it does not apply to the publisher under test. The runner must itself comply: on a repeated non-zero Hop ID in a publisher announcement it closes the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (session 0x3) and records the message; repeated 0 entries are accepted. Following the receiver-close convention of draft 22 (D22-4-2-MUST-109) and L06-5-1-1-MUST-037, this close rule is not turned into a publisher rule; a publisher announcement with a duplicate non-zero Hop ID fails to decode and is judged once, by L06-7-4-MUST-139.

requirements.summary: A relay adding a declared Cost to Route Costs saturates each sum at the largest variable-length integer.
requirements.rationale: Binds a forwarding relay that adds costs; an origin seeds its Route Costs with its production cost and adds nothing, and the runner forwards nothing.

requirements.summary: A receiver treats a missing Cold Route Cost (from a bridged or older peer) as the saturation ceiling, not as 0.
requirements.rationale: Binds the receiver of announcements, which is the runner, and only for bridged or pre-06 peers; a moq-lite-06 publisher always carries the Cold cost field. The runner must itself comply if it ever ranks routes from such a peer (it does not in L1).

requirements.summary: After an ANNOUNCE_END retires an Announce ID, the publisher never references that id again on the stream.
requirements.rationale: Observable by decoding the publisher's Announce Stream, but only once a route is retracted. In l06-announce-lifecycle the runner holds an ANNOUNCE_REQUEST for the broadcast's prefix open while the adapter or driver ends the publisher's broadcast and starts it again (if the target supports that within one session), for a stated window. The evaluator tracks assigned and retired ids (each ANNOUNCE_START assigns the next id): an ANNOUNCE_END or ANNOUNCE_UPDATE naming a retired id is a Fail. With no ANNOUNCE_END in the window (for example the moq CLI ending its session with the broadcast) the row is NotRun, never a Pass. The scenario needs the adapter or driver to end and restart a broadcast within one session, which the adapter contract does not offer yet (an L1d/L1e item); until it does the row is NotRun, never a Pass. References to never-assigned ids and a fresh id on re-announcement are recorded as information (not keyword rules). An ANNOUNCE message with an unknown Type is not judged here: moq.dev skips it by Message Length while the L1b decoder returns InvalidValue, and that decision is open for the L1d session layer (handoff.from_L1b DEFERRED (b)); until it is made such a message is recorded and the stream is inconclusive for this row from that point on, never a Fail.

requirements.summary: An ANNOUNCE_UPDATE may carry a Hop ID list different from the route's original one.
requirements.rationale: A permission with nothing to fail. The l06-announce-* evaluators must accept a changed Hop ID list (and a cost-only change) in an ANNOUNCE_UPDATE for a live id.

requirements.summary: A subscriber does not reuse a Subscribe ID within a session, even after the earlier subscription closed.
requirements.rationale: The subscriber chooses Subscribe IDs; the runner plays it. The runner must itself comply: every SUBSCRIBE in a session (probes included) gets a new id, which also keeps GROUP attribution by Subscribe ID unambiguous for the group evaluators.

requirements.summary: During congestion a publisher sends higher Subscriber Priority values first.
requirements.rationale: A publisher obligation, but priority is out of the L1 scope (design spec: L2), and it needs controlled congestion that the L1 runner does not create; on an uncongested path any order is conforming.

requirements.summary: A publisher resets Group Streams for non-latest groups older than the subscription's Subscriber Max Age.
requirements.rationale: A publisher obligation, but max-age expiry is out of the L1 scope (design spec: L2) and depends on timestamps and Timescale from TRACK_INFO (7.12, L2). The L1 evaluators must accept such resets: a Group stream reset by the publisher is not a Fail.

requirements.summary: A publisher may keep groups that are stale for live delivery for FETCH or later subscriptions.
requirements.rationale: A permission with nothing to fail; retention is only visible through FETCH (L2).

requirements.summary: A publisher starts a subscription at the oldest group at or above the floor that Section 6.2 has not expired.
requirements.rationale: Which groups are unexpired depends on the publisher's retention and on Section 6.2 timing (Publisher Max Age in TRACK_INFO, L2), and reaching back is best-effort; the runner cannot know which groups the publisher still holds, so a later start cannot be shown to be a deviation. The hard bound (never older than the floor) is L06-7-9-MUST-NOT-159.

requirements.summary: A publisher never delivers a group older than the subscription's Group Start floor.
requirements.rationale: In l06-subscribe-group-floor the runner first learns the latest Group Sequence L from a default subscription in the same session, then opens two floored subscriptions with new Subscribe IDs: Group Start F = L and F = L + 2 (a floor above the latest group, which simply waits), Frame Start 0, Group End 0, and a large Subscriber Max Age; the values are recorded. A floor of 0 is no floor, so the F = L case needs L >= 1; when the latest group is 0 that subscription is NotRun (the F = L + 2 case still runs). For each, any Group stream whose GROUP names that Subscribe ID with a Group Sequence below the floor is a Fail. The draft is inconsistent on the Group Start encoding: Section 3.6 (draft 414-416) and moq.dev (lite/subscribe.rs decode_start_group) carry the raw floor, while draft 2056-2058 says Group Start is offset by 1. The evaluator uses the raw floor F; a value of exactly F-1 (compliant only under the offset reading) is recorded as the reading conflict and makes the row inconclusive (NotRun) rather than a Fail, and only a value below F-1, wrong under both readings, is a Fail. A subscription with no decoded Group stream in the stated window (seconds, long enough for two groups at the target's cadence) is NotRun, never a Pass. The runner must itself send only conforming floors (Frame Start 0, Frame End 0).

requirements.summary: A subscriber that has received no group sends Frame Start 0.
requirements.rationale: Binds the subscriber; the runner plays it. Restates L06-3-6-MUST-021: the runner sends a non-zero Frame Start only for a group it has received (the abutting probe of L06-3-6-MUST-020).

requirements.summary: A SUBSCRIBE carries Frame End 0 whenever its Group End is 0.
requirements.rationale: Binds the sender of SUBSCRIBE, the subscriber; the runner plays it. Restates L06-3-6-MUST-022: the runner complies except in the named probe of L06-3-6-MUST-023, which judges the publisher's reset.

requirements.summary: A subscriber may send several SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE messages for one subscription.
requirements.rationale: A permission of the subscriber; the runner plays it. The draft gives the publisher no keyword obligation for SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE in this section.

requirements.summary: Every TRACK_INFO field is fixed for the lifetime of the Track and must not change.
requirements.rationale: The runner opens two Track Streams for the same track, the second after a short pause, and the evaluator compares every TRACK_INFO the publisher sent for the track in the context. Every field of every reply must be identical: Publisher Priority, Publisher Max Age and Timescale. Any difference is a Fail. Fewer than two TRACK_INFO replies for the track make the row NotRun. A track that was not announced or does not exist is answered with a reset (draft 5.1.4), which is not a reply. The unlimited maximum age the moq CLI sends as 2^53-1 is a number like any other here (candidate divergence P6 is recorded in the punch list, not scored).

requirements.summary: Subscriber properties fan in at a relay and may change freely through SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE.
requirements.rationale: Rationale for why only publisher properties are immutable. The permission is the subscriber's to change its own properties with SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE; the runner may send SUBSCRIBE_UPDATE (L1d does) and nothing in the publisher is constrained by it.

requirements.summary: A subscriber may issue a SUBSCRIBE or FETCH with an older Group Start.
requirements.rationale: The permission is the subscriber's: the runner may ask for an older group. The consequence for the publisher (it may already have dropped it) is L06-7-12-MAY-166, and the runner's FETCH scenarios accept a reset for a group the publisher no longer holds.

requirements.summary: A publisher may have already dropped any group whose age exceeds Publisher Max Age.
requirements.rationale: A permission: a publisher that still holds an old group is conforming, so there is nothing to fail. l06-fetch-group therefore asks only for the groups a subscription has just delivered, and l06-fetch-unknown-group accepts only a reset, never a served group, for a group that never existed.

requirements.summary: A publisher may drop groups sooner than Publisher Max Age under resource pressure.
requirements.rationale: A permission; a publisher that never drops early is conforming. See L06-7-12-MUST-NOT-168 for the subscriber side.

requirements.summary: Subscribers must not assume that older groups within the Publisher Max Age bound are still available.
requirements.rationale: A subscriber duty: the runner plays the subscriber. It never turns a reset or an absent older group into a Fail of the publisher when the group is older than the newest one received: l06-fetch-group asks for a group just delivered (and treats a reset as NotRun, not as a Fail), and the only reset it requires is for a group that never existed (L06-5-1-3-MUST-066).

requirements.summary: A Publisher Max Age of 0 means the publisher caches only the latest group, and older groups may be dropped as soon as a newer one arrives.
requirements.rationale: A permission attached to the value 0; a publisher that keeps more is conforming. The runner reads the value as data and never expects a reset for an older group because of it.

requirements.summary: The Timescale in TRACK_INFO must be non-zero.
requirements.rationale: Judged on every TRACK_INFO the publisher sent in the context: a Timescale of 0 is a Fail. The codec decodes the value as sent and the evaluator judges it (the reader raises no issue for it). No TRACK_INFO reply makes the row NotRun. This is the publisher's half of the sentence; the subscriber's reaction to 0 is L06-7-12-MUST-171.

requirements.summary: A subscriber that receives a Timescale of 0 resets the stream with a protocol violation.
requirements.rationale: A subscriber duty: the runner plays the subscriber for probing only and is a passive recorder (see L06-5-1-4-MUST-069). When l06-track-info meets a zero Timescale it is a Fail of the publisher for L06-7-12-MUST-170 and the runner leaves the Track Stream as the publisher closed it. Recorded as a known runner gap in docs/interop-notes.md.

requirements.summary: The Group in SUBSCRIBE_OK is greater than or equal to the subscription's requested start group.
requirements.rationale: Judged on the same floored subscriptions as L06-7-9-MUST-NOT-159 but from a different message: the SUBSCRIBE_OK decoded with the L1b codec (Type 0x0, one Group varint). A Group below the requested floor is a Fail. The draft is inconsistent on the Group Start encoding: Section 3.6 (draft 414-416) and moq.dev (lite/subscribe.rs decode_start_group) carry the raw floor, while draft 2056-2058 says Group Start is offset by 1. The evaluator uses the raw floor F; a value of exactly F-1 (compliant only under the offset reading) is recorded as the reading conflict and makes the row inconclusive (NotRun) rather than a Fail, and only a value below F-1, wrong under both readings, is a Fail. When the latest group L is 0 the F = L subscription has no floor (F = 0) and is NotRun for this row; F must be at least 1. A default subscription (no floor) cannot violate the rule and is not judged. A floored subscription with no SUBSCRIBE_OK in the stated window is NotRun (the publisher may withhold SUBSCRIBE_OK until a group resolves the start, or refuse with a reset). Whether the first Group stream matches the SUBSCRIBE_OK Group is recorded as information.

requirements.summary: A subscriber does not wait for any group at or after the SUBSCRIBE_END Group.
requirements.rationale: Binds the subscriber; the runner plays it. The runner must itself comply: the group evaluators stop expecting groups at or after SUBSCRIBE_END.Group (an exclusive bound) and never count them as missing.

requirements.summary: After SUBSCRIBE_END a publisher may still send SUBSCRIBE_DROP for groups below the end it cannot deliver.
requirements.rationale: A permission with nothing to fail. The subscribe and group evaluators must accept SUBSCRIBE_DROP after SUBSCRIBE_END for groups below its Group.

requirements.summary: SUBSCRIBE_DROP may arrive at any point after the subscription opens, including after SUBSCRIBE_END.
requirements.rationale: A permission with nothing to fail. The subscribe and group evaluators must accept SUBSCRIBE_DROP before SUBSCRIBE_OK, between groups and after SUBSCRIBE_END.

requirements.summary: The subscriber must already have the track's TRACK_INFO to parse the FETCH response frames.
requirements.rationale: A subscriber duty: the runner plays the subscriber. The runner opens a Track Stream for the track and keeps the TRACK_INFO before it FETCHes or reads frames on that track. The same duty is L06-5-1-3-MUST-067 in section 5.1.3.

requirements.summary: A publisher holding fewer frames than requested resets the Fetch Stream rather than truncating the response.
requirements.rationale: The runner subscribes to the track and records one Group stream that completed (FIN, no reset) with N frames, so the publisher demonstrably held at least those N frames. It then FETCHes that group three ways on separate Fetch Streams: whole group (Frame Start 0, Frame End 0), a leading range (Frame Start 0, Frame End 2, i.e. frames 0 and 1), and a trailing range (Frame Start 1, Frame End 0). Each reply must be exactly the requested frames then FIN, or a RESET_STREAM (the publisher may have dropped the group, 7.12). A FIN after fewer frames than the reference group holds for that range is a Fail (the truncation),. A range answered with more frames than requested is not a truncation and gives no verdict for that range (a different defect, not this row); the frames are compared by count only, and the row passes when at least one range came back exact and no range came back short. A reference group that did not complete, or a fetch the publisher left unanswered inside the window, makes the row NotRun. A group that really ends before Frame End is not a truncation (7.16), so the ranges never ask beyond N (a range that does not fit a reference group of fewer than 3 frames is not sent). Judged on groups the publisher holds, so it never shares evidence with L06-5-1-3-MUST-066.

requirements.summary: A GOAWAY New Session URI must not exceed 8,192 bytes.
requirements.rationale: The sender's duty. The publisher under test would only send a GOAWAY on its own initiative, and the moq CLI never sends one (source survey), so a runner cannot provoke the observation; a scripted publisher exercises it in L2b. The runner itself never sends a URI above the limit except in the named violation probe l06-goaway-oversize, which exists to judge the receiver (L06-7-18-MUST-179).

requirements.summary: A receiver treats a GOAWAY URI longer than 8,192 bytes as a protocol violation.
requirements.rationale: The runner opens a Goaway Stream whose message carries a New Session URI length prefix of 8193 followed by 8193 URI bytes (a named deliberate violation; the draft lets the receiver reject on the prefix alone, L06-7-18-MAY-180, so both the prefix and the body are sent). The wording is a protocol violation, which is a session error: the publisher must close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (0x3). A close with another code, no close, or a reset of only the Goaway Stream is a Fail (the moq CLI only logs an oversize URI, candidate defect P8). A close that precedes the oversize GOAWAY is not its reaction and is NotRun, as is a transport failure.

requirements.summary: A receiver may reject an oversize GOAWAY URI based on the length prefix alone.
requirements.rationale: A permission about when to reject; a receiver that reads the whole URI first is conforming. l06-goaway-oversize sends the whole URI so both kinds of receiver are judged by their reaction only.

requirements.summary: A recipient must validate the GOAWAY URI against local policy before reconnecting, verifying scheme, authority and port.
requirements.rationale: Reconnect policy of the application; observing it needs a redirect target the runner controls and a publisher that follows redirects. The moq CLI logs the URI and keeps the session (source survey), so there is nothing to observe. The runner itself never reconnects to a GOAWAY URI. L2b, with a scripted publisher.

requirements.summary: If URI validation fails the recipient must close the session without reconnecting.
requirements.rationale: Depends on L06-7-18-MUST-181 and on a publisher that validates and reconnects; the moq CLI does neither. L2b, with a scripted publisher.

requirements.summary: A client must send an empty GOAWAY New Session URI.
requirements.rationale: The publisher is the QUIC client. It would have to send a GOAWAY first, which the moq CLI never does (source survey), so a runner cannot provoke the observation; a scripted publisher exercises it in L2b. The runner is the server, which is allowed a non-empty URI.

requirements.summary: A server that receives a non-empty GOAWAY New Session URI must close the session with a protocol violation.
requirements.rationale: A server duty and the runner is the server. A publisher client never sends a GOAWAY (see L06-7-18-MUST-183), so the runner never receives a URI to refuse. Known runner gap, recorded in docs/interop-notes.md: if a publisher did send one the runner would record it as a decoded message and not close.

requirements.summary: The new session URI should use the same scheme as the current session's URI.
requirements.rationale: The sender's preference. The publisher never sends a GOAWAY here, so it cannot be observed; the runner's own GOAWAY URI keeps the scheme of the session URL it was given.

requirements.summary: An endpoint must close the session with a protocol violation if it receives more than one GOAWAY.
requirements.rationale: The runner opens a Goaway Stream with a valid GOAWAY (empty URI, so the first message is legitimate), waits for a settle interval, then opens a second Goaway Stream with another GOAWAY. The publisher must close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (0x3), as the sentence says (a session close, not a stream reset). A close before the second GOAWAY was written is not the reaction to it and is NotRun. That includes a publisher that closes the session on the first GOAWAY: a graceful shutdown on a GOAWAY is allowed (5.1.6), so it cannot be told apart from a reaction to the second. A second GOAWAY left unanswered through the window is a Fail. The wording says nothing about two messages on one stream, so the runner uses two streams.

requirements.summary: A peer that reconnects to a provided URI should keep using that URI for later reconnects.
requirements.rationale: Reconnect behaviour across sessions; the runner would need a publisher that reconnects (the moq CLI does not follow redirects) and several connections to observe. L2b.

requirements.summary: A relay that receives a GOAWAY should treat that session's announcements as the most expensive routes.
requirements.rationale: A relay duty. The publisher under test is an origin and the runner is not a relay.

requirements.summary: A broadcast reachable only over a draining session must keep being served until the session ends.
requirements.rationale: A relay duty (routes are the relay's). The publisher under test is an origin; the runner is not a relay. The origin publisher's own side, to keep serving existing streams after a GOAWAY, is not required by this sentence and is observed only as the absence of new streams (L06-5-1-6-MUST-NOT-077).

requirements.summary: A track's Group Sequence increases by 1 for each new group.
requirements.rationale: Judged on the default subscription of l06-subscribe-latest, which states a large Subscriber Max Age (as in L06-7-9-MUST-NOT-159, recorded in the evidence) so staleness resets cannot explain a gap; with a small Max Age an unaccounted gap is inconclusive, not a Fail. It is judged over the window stated for L06-6-3-2-MUST-093. The evaluator orders the decoded GROUP sequences of the subscription and requires them to form a consecutive run; a gap is accounted for when a SUBSCRIBE_DROP range covers it, and makes the row inconclusive when a Group stream of the subscription was reset before its GROUP decoded. An unaccounted gap is a Fail of this SHOULD row (the only evaluator that fails on a gap alone; L06-7-19-MUST-191 requires every other group evaluator to tolerate one), flagged as inferred from delivery (a group skipped in delivery without a SUBSCRIBE_DROP looks like a numbering gap; on a loopback path congestion is unlikely; the evidence keeps the gap). Fewer than two decoded groups is NotRun.

requirements.summary: A subscriber handles gaps in Group Sequence.
requirements.rationale: Binds the subscriber; the runner plays it. The runner must itself comply: a gap is never a session error and no group evaluator fails on a gap alone except L06-7-19-SHOULD-190, which judges only numbering gaps inferred from delivery.

requirements.summary: A subscriber does not assume that frames before a GROUP's non-zero Frame Start will arrive on another stream.
requirements.rationale: Binds the subscriber; the runner plays it. The runner must itself comply: leading frames missing from a Group stream with a non-zero Frame Start are a gap, not expected elsewhere, unless the runner opened a separate subscription covering them (as the abutting probe of L06-3-6-MUST-020 does).
